coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion in the run’s scope was checked, not merely sampled: the mapped test body was read in scripts/acceptance*.mjs and then the assertion’s observable was re-executed independently (grading/evidence/checklist-api.json, checklist-ui.json, m8-independent.json, m1-duplicates.json). No mapping was found to claim an observable its test does not exercise. Strikes are declared consistently in the manifest and match ENVIRONMENT.md item by item, and the one grader-class assertion the lane could not satisfy (m5-a01) is carried in knownGaps as status "platform-gap" rather than mapped to a passing test. Two weaknesses worth recording, neither dishonest: (1) m1-a08 maps to profile-edit-persists, which asserts the bio but not the display name the assertion also names — the grader verified display-name persistence independently and it passes; (2) m2-a12 maps to a test asserting a role=link element, which does not itself prove the system browser opens — source inspection confirms onPressLink={Linking.openURL}. The lane’s copied choreography harness was diffed against the frozen instrument: the only changes are the disclosed fixture-path relocation, an AJV import fix, and explicit struck-media skips (required=false, pass=null); no assertion, timing ceiling, receipt emitter or green-aggregation rule was altered, and evidence/instrument-repairs.md describes exactly those diffs.

defects.summary: Message receipt-row updates never reach an already-established local replica in a group conversation, so the sender’s receipt indicator stays at `sent` indefinitely — including across a page reload — while the server has recorded delivered/read.
defects.evidence: grading/evidence/group-ui-receipt.json (3/3 trials: transitions pending -> sent only, then no change for 25 s); grading/evidence/group-server-state.json (all three messages: carol=delivered, bob=read, so the correct aggregate was `delivered`); grading/evidence/fresh-group-receipt.json (reproduced in a group created seconds earlier: UI `sent`, server bob=read/carol=delivered, still `sent` after reload, correct `delivered` from a clean browser profile); grading/evidence/m3-choreo.jsonl (2 grader runs, both failed the required group-receipt check). trace.md §M3 group aggregate receipt.

defects.summary: Live reaction propagation through the UI write path is unreliable: setting or clearing a reaction intermittently never becomes visible on the peer client, while the same operations driven through the API propagate in ~100-320 ms.
defects.evidence: grading/evidence/reaction-ui.json (UI-driven, 3 trials: trial 1 removal never observed within 10 s, trial 3 set never observed within 10 s, trial 2 removal 3666 ms); grading/evidence/reaction-live.json (API-driven control, 3/3 trials clean: add 107-257 ms, replace ~311 ms, clear ~210 ms); grading/evidence/m4-choreo.jsonl plus the first grader M4 run (1 of 6 harness attempts across two runs passed; a stale ❤️ chip stayed visible with aria-label "❤️ 1" after removal). trace.md §M4 live reactions.

defects.summary: A push payload is permanently dropped, never re-emitted, for any message sent within roughly 10-12 s of an abrupt client disconnect, because the recipient’s stale presence lease suppresses emission and nothing revisits the decision once the lease expires.
defects.evidence: grading/evidence/push-lease.json: with no client, a push row is emitted; at t+1 s, t+5 s and t+9 s after an abrupt context close no row is emitted, at t+13 s and t+18 s emission resumes, and re-checking the three suppressed messages 20 s later shows no retroactive emission. This is also the mechanism behind the single builder-suite failure observed under grading (m6 offline-recipient-push-outbox ran 1.1 s after the M5 segment closed its browser and failed; it passed on the protocol re-run). trace.md §M6 push.

defects.summary: Live two-client updates intermittently miss the harness’s 10 s settlement budget across several surfaces (follow projection, repost attribution, repost-on-Following), so individual attempts fail where best-of-3 then passes.
defects.evidence: grading/evidence/m2-choreo.jsonl: m2/follow-unfollow-live-projection attempt 1 = 10441.9 ms fail then 291.8/288.3 ms pass; m2/repost-toggle-live-attribution attempts 1-2 pass then attempt 3 = 10187.2 ms fail; m2/repost-following-feed-surface attempt 2 fail. Machine load averages during these runs were 17-25 on an 18-core shared host (recorded per run in trace.md), so part of this is environmental; it is recorded as a reliability observation rather than a correctness failure.

defects.summary: /q/history returns fewer rows than the documented page size (32 of a documented 50) with complete:false and no continuation cursor, so a correct client cannot distinguish a short page from the end of history without the documented caveat.
defects.evidence: grading/evidence/api-m1a07-m6a12.json: history page 1 returned 32 rows, complete=false, next=null. API.md documents exactly this case ("false without a continuation indicates a platform execution bound, not an empty complete history"), so the behaviour is disclosed rather than surprising; recorded as cosmetic because the documentation carries the reader through it.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), nearer 90.
O1.justification: Of the 119 in-scope assertions (M1-M8), 28 are struck-by-environment, leaving 91 live. 80 pass under independent grader execution, 2 fail (m3-a09, m5-a01) and 9 are not-run because M7 is a separate session excluded by ENVIRONMENT.md and so scores not-passed per the applicability rule. M1, M2, M4, M6 and M8 reproduce complete under grading; M3 loses only the group aggregate receipt and M5 only the server-side expiry refusal. Above 60 because no later milestone is patchy — M5, M6 and M8 are as solid as M1-M4, including all seven M8 analytics assertions verified against a grader-recomputed corpus. Short of 90 because one full milestone checklist (M7, 9 assertions) is not passed at all, one failure is a stated security guarantee, and the platform-proof (simulator) artifacts the 90 anchor names do not exist in this run, though they are struck rather than missing.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ("multiple high-severity defects in core flows") and the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path"), slightly below 60.
O2.justification: Two major defects (d-01, d-02) sit in core messaging flows rather than off the happy path: group receipt indicators never advance on an established replica, and UI-driven reaction changes intermittently never reach the peer. That is worse than 60’s "off the happy path" framing. It is better than 30 because no defect corrupts or loses data, none crashes the app, and in both cases the server state is verifiably correct — these are client liveness failures with sound persistence underneath. Three lesser findings (d-03 push loss in a bounded window, d-04 intermittent settlement misses partly attributable to load averages of 17-25 on a shared host, d-05 a documented short page) add weight without changing the band.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush") and the 90 anchor ("reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof — on full runs including M8’s durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence").
O4.justification: Scored only from choreography receipts produced by grader-driven runs. Everything observable behaves as specced: m6/offline-message-queue-flush-in-order passed (two offline messages showed pending state, flushed in order on reconnect in 2076 ms and reached read); m5/warm-offline-search-over-synced-messages passed with connectivity cut and no restart; m8/m8-a15-dual-offline-convergence passed (two warm-offline same-account clients each queued a message and converged in server-arrival order with no loss and no duplicates, 823.6/1791 ms) and m8/m8-a16-dual-offline-receipts passed. The grader also observed correct offline behaviour outside the harness: an expired message vanished from offline in-chat and global search after the client synced the expiry. Well above 60 — nothing is lost, mis-ordered, or receipt-wrong after flush. Held below 90 because the 90 anchor requires the native proof including M8’s durable-queue restart, and no simulator artifact exists: ENVIRONMENT.md does not require one and the lane claims none. The honesty clause of this dimension is satisfied strongly rather than strained — README.md and platform-gaps.md both state plainly that native behaviour has bundle-compilation evidence only and that no native runtime persistence proof is claimed, so there is no gap between claim and guarantee to penalise.

O5.bandRationale: First-match in the order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: the invariant manifest conforms under grader-independent verification (grading/evidence/scale-verify-grader.json — 28 checks over the retained scale-instance store, every per-entity count exact, the pinned scale.log sha256 b26bf1ae… and both checkpoint prefix digests matching instrument/fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json, settledPrefix 167157 = full action count, failedActions 0) and the replay used 209.4 s of its 14400 s cap (1.45%), so the cap was not exhausted. The only manifest deviations are per-chat and named message counts, and grading/evidence/strike-accounting.json shows all 901 of them are exactly the struck send-media actions in that chat, summing to precisely 910 = the manifest’s mediaMessages and the receipt’s struckMediaMessages — including the named g0001 fixture’s shortfall of exactly its 10 struck media messages. ENVIRONMENT.md authorises recording media-dependent invariants as struck-by-environment, so this is not a named-fixture mismatch. Band 30 fires: the frozen degradation rule "Following-feed load for the 500-follow probe user ≤ 3× the same query for a 5-follow user" fails. Grader-run, sequential, k=20 after 3 warm-ups, interleaved over 3 rounds to neutralise load drift, both queries returning 20-row first pages: p95 ratios 8.98×, 11.53× and 10.07× against a 3× limit, best-of-3 = 8.98× (grading/evidence/o5-feed-rule.json). The lane’s own recorded probe data agrees (23.65 ms vs 1.45 ms = 16×). The two other re-measurable ratio rules pass (deep paging page 50 vs page 1 = 0.96×; celebrity read path = 1.40×), no probe timed out, errored or OOMed, and absolute latencies are healthy throughout (every p95 ≤ 55 ms), so this is a growth-shape failure and not a viability failure — but the rule is frozen and hardware-independent, and it fails. Recorded limits: the wave committed no rotated probe set, so these are grader-authored substitutes; the celebrity write path and the 50-member-group receipt-stall rule were not re-measured because they require writes and the scale corpus was kept read-only; and the mid-curve 10%/50% comparisons for search, Insights and Trending are not reproducible once replay has completed. Absolute p95 ceilings are "pilot-calibrated" placeholders in this instrument snapshot, so no ceiling can be exceeded (band 60’s first clause) and no ceiling utilisation can be affirmed as ≤50% (band 90’s condition) — but both are moot, band 30 having already matched.

notes: RUN DEVIATIONS (recorded by the grading wrapper, not by the frozen prompt). (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave: execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the sentinel "none-uncommitted", and probeResults is empty. No probes were invented. Because applicability.json makes O3 scorable "from the wave’s secret rotated holdout probes only", O3 is recorded null despite its predicate (M6 green plus M1-M5 attempted) being satisfied — its sole sanctioned input does not exist, and scoring it from other evidence would contradict the manifest. O5 is band-mapped as the manifest requires, using grader-authored substitute probes that are labelled as such in its rationale. (2) The claude family has not passed the calibration gate, so grader.calibrationPassed is false and this grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader; sameFamilyGraded is false (the builder harness recorded in milestone-record.json is a non-claude family). (3) Timing-sensitive checks were judged best-of-3 with machine load recorded beside each measurement in trace.md; the host was heavily shared throughout, with 1-minute load averages between 10 and 166 on 18 cores. (4) grader.rerunsUsed=1 records the one protocol re-run of a failed phase (the M6 builder-suite segment); it was not a grader-tooling abort.
